source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with Reye's syndrome is admitted. Which nursing action is the PRIORITY?
options: Keep the room quiet with dim lights
questions.rationale: Cerebral edema progresses in Reye's syndrome, so maintaining cerebral perfusion and controlling ICP is the priority. Reducing environmental stimuli lowers stress on brain tissue.
explanations: Correct: reduces stimuli that raise ICP.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1164 (PDF p. 1451)
questions.quote: A priority component of care for a child with Reye’s syndrome is maintaining effective cerebral perfusion and controlling intracranial pressure.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes cerebral palsy?
options: An infection of the central nervous system
Brain inflammation after a viral illness
Chronic difficulty controlling muscles from a motor-system abnormality
A chromosomal disorder with intellectual disability
questions.rationale: Cerebral palsy is a chronic disability with difficulty controlling the muscles because of an abnormality in the pyramidal or extrapyramidal motor system. Meningitis is an infection, and encephalitis is inflammation.
explanations: Correct: the definition of cerebral palsy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1165 (PDF p. 1452)
questions.quote: Cerebral palsy is a chronic disability that is characterized by difficulty with controlling the muscles because of an abnormality in the extrapyramidal or pyramidal motor system.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which characteristic is PRIMARY in autism spectrum disorder?
options: Normal social play that stops at age 5
Lack of social interaction and awareness
questions.rationale: Autism begins in infancy or toddlerhood, and its primary characteristic is a lack of social interaction and awareness. Imitation and social play are absent or abnormal, and verbal communication is impaired.
explanations: Social play is absent or abnormal from the start.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1166 (PDF p. 1453)
questions.quote: A primary characteristic is a lack of social interaction and awareness.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with leukemia is starting chemotherapy. Which intervention belongs in the care plan?
options: Check the mouth and anus each shift for breakdown
Use a firm toothbrush for oral care
questions.rationale: The mouth and anus are checked each shift for ulcers or breakdown. Rectal temperatures are avoided, and bland, nonirritating foods are given.
explanations: Rectal temperatures risk injury and infection.
Correct: early detection of mucosal breakdown.
A soft swab or brush is used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1169 (PDF p. 1456)
questions.quote: the nurse should assess the mouth and anus each shift for ulcers, erythema, or breakdown.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with leukemia has a platelet count of 20,000/mm3. Which intervention should be AVOIDED?
options: Cleaning the mouth with soft swabs
questions.rationale: With this low platelet count, the child is at risk for bleeding. Rectal temperatures and suppositories are avoided; stools are checked for blood and soft swabs are used for mouth care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1302 (PDF p. 1603)
questions.quote: Taking rectal temperatures and the use of suppositories are avoided because of the risk of rectal bleeding.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How should an infant be positioned after pyloromyotomy?
options: Prone with the head of the bed raised
questions.rationale: After pyloromyotomy, the head of the bed is raised and the infant placed prone to reduce the risk of aspiration, unless the surgeon orders otherwise.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1187 (PDF p. 1479)
questions.quote: After pyloromyotomy, the head of the bed is elevated, and the infant is placed prone to reduce the risk of aspiration.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Rico, 10, is admitted in vaso-occlusive pain crisis from sickle cell anemia.
questions.stem: Which prescription should the nurse question?
questions.rationale: Meperidine is contraindicated for ongoing pain because of the risk of seizures. Strong opioids such as morphine or hydromorphone are used, along with fluids, oxygen, and rest.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1189 (PDF p. 1481)
questions.quote: Meperidine hydrochloride is contraindicated for ongoing pain management because of the increased risk of seizures

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which position reduces stridor in an infant with laryngomalacia?
questions.rationale: The prone position with the neck hyperextended improves breathing in laryngomalacia. A child in respiratory difficulty is never left unattended.
explanations: Without hyperextension it is less effective.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1190 (PDF p. 1482)
questions.quote: The prone position with the neck hyperextended improves the child’s breathing.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant has an occipital encephalocele. Which item helps position the infant without pressure on the sac?
questions.rationale: A foam half-donut keeps pressure off an occipital encephalocele. The other items do not protect the lesion.
explanations: Correct: relieves pressure on the sac.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1193 (PDF p. 1485)
questions.quote: If the encephalocele is in the occipital area, a foam half donut may be useful for positioning to prevent this pressure.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of a child with hepatitis B calls because the jaundice seems worse. What should the nurse tell her?
options: 'Jaundice can look worse before it clears.'
'Bring your child to the ER now.'
questions.rationale: Jaundice may appear to worsen before it resolves. Parents are taught the true danger signs: changes in neurologic status, bleeding, and fluid retention.
explanations: Not needed unless danger signs appear.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1195 (PDF p. 1487)
questions.quote: The parents should be instructed that jaundice may appear to get worse before it resolves.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding BEST shows that a gluten-free diet is working for a child with celiac disease?
options: The child is free of diarrhea
The child has no bloody stools
The child tolerates wheat and rye
questions.rationale: Watery diarrhea is a frequent sign of celiac disease, so its absence shows effective treatment. Bloody stools are not part of the disease.
explanations: Correct: diarrhea resolves with the diet.
Not a feature of celiac disease.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1217 (PDF p. 1510)
questions.quote: The absence of diarrhea indicates effective treatment.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has strabismus of the LEFT eye. Which statement shows the mother understands patching?
questions.rationale: The good (right) eye is patched to force use of the weak (left) eye. Patching works best during the preschool years.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1221 (PDF p. 1514)
questions.quote: With this treatment, the good eye is patched; this encourages the child to use the weaker eye.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which intervention in a care plan for an infant with congestive heart failure needs revision?
options: Elevate the head of the bed
Limit the time for each feeding
Wake the infant hourly to check vital signs
questions.rationale: Measures that reduce cardiac workload include elevating the head, limiting feeding time, uninterrupted rest, and oxygen during stress. Waking the infant often is not therapeutic.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1247 (PDF p. 1543)
questions.quote: Measures that will decrease the workload on the heart include limiting the time that the infant is allowed to bottle-feed or breast-feed

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which action by a student caring for a child with a head injury needs correction?
options: Keeping the child awake as ordered
questions.rationale: Forcing fluids can cause fluid overload and raise ICP. Neurologic checks, an upright position for drainage, and keeping the child awake for assessment are appropriate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1292 (PDF p. 1593)
questions.quote: Forcing fluids may cause fluid overload and increased ICP.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is associated with hydrocephalus in a 6-month-old?
questions.rationale: A bulging anterior fontanel reflects increased CSF in the ventricles. Infants also have thin, widely separated skull bones.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1332 (PDF p. 1634)
questions.quote: A bulging anterior fontanel indicates an increase in cerebrospinal fluid collection in the cerebral ventricle

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother asks what Kawasaki disease is. The nurse explains that it is:
options: A chronic autoimmune disease of connective tissue
A febrile generalized vasculitis of unknown cause
A reaction to a strep throat infection
questions.rationale: Kawasaki disease (mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a febrile generalized vasculitis of unknown cause. Its most serious complication is cardiac involvement, including coronary aneurysms.
explanations: Correct: the definition of Kawasaki disease.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1338 (PDF p. 1641)
questions.quote: Kawasaki disease, also called mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome, is a febrile generalized vasculitis of unknown etiology.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a child with iron deficiency anemia ask which foods have iron the body absorbs MOST easily. The nurse recommends:
questions.rationale: Iron from meat, poultry, and fish is absorbed most easily. Vegetables, fruits, cereals, and breads contain iron that is harder to absorb.
explanations: Correct: heme iron is easily absorbed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1339 (PDF p. 1642)
questions.quote: Dietary sources of iron that are easy for the body to absorb include meat, poultry, and fish.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement describes patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)?
options: A defect in the atrial septum
questions.rationale: The ductus arteriosus connects the aorta and pulmonary artery in fetal life and normally closes after birth. If it stays open, blood shunts from the high-pressure aorta to the pulmonary artery (left-to-right shunt).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1340 (PDF p. 1643)
questions.quote: Patent ductus arteriosus is described as an artery that connects the aorta and the pulmonary artery during fetal life.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is consistent with congenital hypothyroidism in an infant?
options: A hoarse cry and excessive sleeping
questions.rationale: Congenital hypothyroidism can cause a hoarse cry, excessive sleeping, bradycardia, constipation, a large tongue and fontanel, hypotonia, prolonged jaundice, and feeding problems.
explanations: The infant is lethargic, not irritable.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1341 (PDF p. 1644)
questions.quote: Other signs and symptoms include prolonged jaundice, lethargy, constipation, feeding problems, coldness to touch, umbilical hernia, hoarse cry, and excessive sleeping.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child's tympanostomy tube falls out at home. What should the nurse tell the parent?
options: 'It's not an emergency, but call the clinic.'
'Push it back into the ear gently.'
questions.rationale: A tube falling out is not an emergency, but the provider should be notified. Parents are shown the tube's size and appearance after surgery.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1344 (PDF p. 1647)
questions.quote: if the tympanostomy tubes fall out, it is not an emergency, but it is best if the primary health care provider or health care clinic is notified.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has a nosebleed. What should the nurse tell the parent to do?
options: Sit up, lean forward, pinch for 10 minutes
questions.rationale: The child sits upright with the head tilted forward so blood does not run into the pharynx. The soft part of the nose is pinched for a full 10 minutes, timed by a clock.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1345 (PDF p. 1648)
questions.quote: The child should be positioned erect, sitting with head tilted forward to avoid blood dripping posteriorly to the pharynx.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: When assessing a child admitted with rheumatic fever, which question is MOST significant?
options: 'Has anyone at home had a sore throat recently?'
'Has your child had a recent vaccine?'
questions.rationale: Rheumatic fever appears 2 to 6 weeks after an untreated or partly treated group A streptococcal throat infection, so the nurse asks about recent sore throats or unexplained fever in the family.
explanations: Correct: identifies a preceding strep infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1346 (PDF p. 1649)
questions.quote: Rheumatic fever characteristically presents 2 to 6 weeks after an untreated or partially treated group A beta-hemolytic streptococcal infection of the respiratory tract.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Parents worry that their son with mumps will develop orchitis. Which sign should the nurse teach them to watch for?
questions.rationale: About a week after parotitis, orchitis begins abruptly with testicular pain and tenderness, fever, chills, headache, and vomiting. It is usually one-sided, and sterility is rare.
explanations: Correct: abrupt fever and testicular pain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1347 (PDF p. 1650)
questions.quote: About 1 week after the appearance of parotitis, there is an abrupt onset of testicular pain, tenderness, fever, chills, headache, and vomiting.
